system.name: CMSwitch
system.one_liner: a compiler that optimizes resource allocation for computing-in-memory accelerators with dynamic compute/memory mode switching

components.name: Dual-mode CIM array
components.role: CIM array capable of switching between memory and compute modes via its driver inputs

components.name: Memory Mode
components.role: operating mode in which the array performs a standard memory read

components.name: Compute Mode
components.role: operating mode in which the array performs in-memory MAC computation

components.name: Memory circuits
components.role: memory-cell array shared by both modes

components.name: Driver
components.role: row/column driver whose GIA/GIAb/IA input signals determine the array's mode

components.name: matrix
components.role: small logic block that changes the driver input to switch modes

components.name: Data IO
components.role: outputs read DATA in memory mode

components.name: PSUM
components.role: outputs the MAC OUTPUT (partial sum) in compute mode

content.key_idea: The same CIM array switches between a memory-read mode and a compute (MAC) mode simply by changing the driver's global input-activation signals, without changing the array itself.
content.reading_order: Left panel (Memory Mode) is read top-to-bottom from Driver through Memory circuits to Data IO/DATA; the eye then crosses the central 'Change Driver INPUT' / matrix block to the mirrored right panel (Compute Mode) ending at PSUM/MAC OUTPUT.

palette.used_for: Memory Mode / Compute Mode header bar fill

style.stroke: thin black/gray borders, dashed outer boundary around the whole dual-mode array
style.arrows: thin solid signal-line arrows between driver and memory circuits

encoding.color_means: dark blue = driver blocks, light gray = memory-circuit cell grid, green = the matrix/control block that switches modes
encoding.line_style_means: dashed outer boundary marks the overall dual-mode array; a vertical divider separates the Memory Mode and Compute Mode panels
encoding.emphasis: the central 'Change Driver INPUT' / matrix block visually bridges the two mirrored mode panels, emphasizing that mode switching is a driver-input change rather than a different array
reusable_patterns: mirrored two-panel diagram sharing a central control block to depict a mode switch

evidence: switching between memory and compute modes of CIM arrays can be achieved by altering the array's driver inputs
CIM arrays perform computations, they enable the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations to be executed entirely within the array

summary: This figure illustrates the dual-mode CIM array that underlies CMSwitch's hardware abstraction: the same physical array can act as either memory or a compute unit depending on its driver input signals. The left panel, labelled Memory Mode, shows a Driver feeding Memory circuits whose GIA/GIAb-controlled READ path produces DATA at the Data IO. A central block, labelled 'Change Driver INPUT' with a small 'matrix' logic box, switches the global input-activation signals. The right panel, labelled Compute Mode, mirrors the same Driver/Memory-circuits layout but with GIA/GIAb/IA signals configured for multiply-accumulate, producing a MAC OUTPUT at the PSUM. The mirrored two-panel layout emphasizes that mode switching is purely a driver-input change, motivating CMSwitch's compiler-level modeling of switching overhead.
summary_zh: 该图展示双模 CIM 阵列：左侧内存模式下驱动器控制存储电路完成读操作输出 DATA；中间通过改变驱动器输入（matrix 模块）切换模式；右侧计算模式下同一阵列执行乘累加并输出 PSUM。
